title: Sample Kit (synthetic, development only)
candidateInstructions: You may use Google Sheets or Excel for anything numerical — share your screen and talk through your reasoning as you go. For code questions, read the snippet and answer verbally. **Show your working.** Ask if a question is unclear.

dimensions.name: Fit with remote / on-call / small-desk model

sections.label: Stage 1 — Intro call
sections.interviewerNotes: Verbal. Not scored 0–3: rate the dimensions 1–5 and write a recommendation.

sections.label: Stage 3 — Take-home marking
sections.interviewerNotes: Mark each criterion 0–3 against the submitted notebook and memo.

questions.title: Walk me through your background
questions.prompt: Give me the two-minute version of your career so far.
questions.whatGoodLooksLike: Concrete — names the systems and numbers they owned. Two minutes means two minutes.

questions.title: Why this role
questions.prompt: Why this role, and why now?
questions.whatGoodLooksLike: Wants ownership and scope; has thought about the growth path.

questions.title: Mean and standard deviation
questions.prompt: Paste these five daily returns (%) into a sheet. Compute the mean and the **sample** standard deviation.

rubric.3: Both numbers, sample stdev named explicitly.
rubric.2: Both numbers, population stdev without a note.

questions.trapOrBonus: Bonus: says five observations say nothing about a strategy.

questions.title: At least one head
questions.prompt: A fair coin is tossed three times. What is the probability of at least one head?

rubric.1: Adds the probabilities (1.5) and notices it is wrong.

questions.trapOrBonus: The trap is adding the probabilities.

questions.title: List vs set
questions.prompt: List vs set — what is the difference, and when would you reach for each?
questions.modelAnswer: A list is an ordered, mutable sequence; a set is unordered membership with O(1) average lookup. Example: a set of seen fill ids for dedup.

questions.title: Correct computations
questions.prompt: The numbers in the submission are correct and computed with sound logic.

rubric.3: Correct with clear reasoning; states assumptions; notices any trap unprompted.
rubric.2: Right idea, minor slip; or correct but needed a nudge.
rubric.1: Partial — some correct components, wrong or missing conclusion.
rubric.0: Wrong, blank, or confidently wrong without reasoning.

questions.title: Clarity of the memo
questions.prompt: Code and memo are readable, assumptions stated, results reproducible.

rubric.3: Correct with clear reasoning; states assumptions; notices any trap unprompted.
rubric.2: Right idea, minor slip; or correct but needed a nudge.
rubric.1: Partial — some correct components, wrong or missing conclusion.
rubric.0: Wrong, blank, or confidently wrong without reasoning.

questions.title: An incident you owned
questions.prompt: Tell us about a time something went wrong in production. What did you do in the first five minutes?
questions.whatGoodLooksLike: Stops the bleeding first, communicates early, fixes the cause, writes it down.
